supporting_observations.claim: Repeated svc-routes logon failures occurred on FILE-COP-01 from 13:36 through 13:51 UTC, generally about once per minute. The events identify FILE-COP-01 as the workstation and 10.52.20.20 as the source address, with status 0xc000006a indicating an incorrect password.

Domain-controller records corroborate failed authentication attempts for svc-routes from FILE-COP-01 during this period; the recorded 4776 failures report status 0xc000006a, and several 4771 events report status 0x18.

The failure pattern is consistent with the scheduled svc-routes password rotation at 13:30 UTC and the job's documented once-per-minute re-authentication: the attempts originate from the job's host and begin shortly after the planned rotation.

At 14:07 UTC, a separate record shows SYSTEM running PowerShell on FILE-COP-01 with explicit credentials targeting svc-routes and DC-COP-01. This is compatible with a manual post-rotation update, but the record alone does not establish the purpose or success of that action.

known_telemetry_limitations: Proxy log collection was unavailable from 13:25 through 14:20 UTC; this limits proxy-based corroboration during the review window.
The provided evidence includes no record demonstrating a successful svc-routes authentication or confirming the RouteSync job's credential update.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish exactly when the password rotation occurred or whether the new password was successfully applied to RouteSync.
The 14:07 PowerShell explicit-credential event does not identify the human operator or prove that it performed the planned job update.
The supplied records do not establish whether any svc-routes authentication succeeded after the failures or whether the account was used for any other activity.
